question.text: Two cells of E.M.F. <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>></mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> are connected in series in the secondary circuit of a potentiometer experiment for determination of E.M.F. The balancing length is found to be <math><mn>825</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. Now when the terminals of cell <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> are reversed, then the balancing length is found to be <math><mn>225</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The ratio of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> is

solution.text:
E2 + E1 = x825

E2 – E1 = x225

Dividing above equations, we get

E2+E1E2-E1=113

Appling componendo and dividendo, we get

E1E2=47
